context:
Goal: the work goes on now, and you can overrule any coordinator pick.
Problem (goal): the coordinator took this undoable pick on Nov 12, 12:26 CST without asking you; it stands unless you choose b.
Based on (ruling): your Nov 12 11:59 CST ruling that every cap end on main opens an issue, cleared or not.
Departs from: main has no such pick on record — the work it governs follows this pick.

lastAnswer.note: id say open an issue too but who reads issues? (your words in chat, 12:58 CST, relayed by the retrospective)

options.gain: No cap end slips past, as your ruling that every cap end opens an issue asks.
options.how: The cap alarm in PR #2745 judges every cancelled run that hit a time cap among the last 100 runs, not only the newest; a cap end in an earlier attempt of a rerun that later passed opens an issue too.
options.label: Keep the pick (Recommended)
options.lose: The other route is not taken unless you choose b.

options.how: Judge only the newest run, and narrow your ruling that every cap end opens an issue to match.
options.label: Overrule it
options.lose: A cap end in an older run in the window goes unreported.

reply: Filed: a, in your words. A cap end in an earlier attempt of a re-run that later passed alarms too. Your 13:07 CST answer to who reads issues (ruling R53): the alarm wakes the batch runner, which fixes it or brings it to the coordinator; no GitHub issue.
short: Cap alarm: every cap end in the window
title: Cap alarm: judge every cancelled cap-end run in the window, not only the newest
why: A coordinator pick you could not see before.
